judge_assessment.explanation: The second hard failure is exact and on its own justifies the REJECT. Problem 3 asks for the zeros "and beside each one state whether the graph crosses the axis or touches and turns there"; verify.json id 3 is a bare zeros check expecting [-3, 1] with no multiplicity or local-shape entry. Problem 5 asks "Which zero has multiplicity two, and what does the graph do there?" and is verified by factor plus zeros only. Problem 7 asks the student to "state the two intervals and their signs" and is verified by two evals (8 and -8) - the requested statement is never checked. Problem 8 asks for "the multiplicity of each" and is verified by factor plus zeros. I would add problem 2, which asks "Does this graph's left end match its right end? Say why in terms of the degree" and carries only two limit checks. I disagree with how the first hard failure is characterised. The judge's error record says the answer key "was not delivered to the user". final_response.md line 3 does name it: "Three PDFs: the student worksheet (10 problems, 5 pages), a step-by-step answer key, and a two-page study guide." The scoring gate flagged it because scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces does a raw substring match for 'answer key' and the markdown is hard-wrapped between the two words, giving 'answer\nkey'. I confirmed this directly: the raw text fails all three answer-key phrases, and after collapsing whitespace it passes. The judge's narrower wording - "with a usable filename or link" - is literally correct, since this response gives no filenames at all where sibling cases print ws_*.pdf / ak_*.pdf / ss_*.pdf. So the verdict stands, but the stated reason conflates a genuine delivery shortfall with a line-wrap artifact in the matcher, and that matcher can produce a hard failure on a response that named the artifact perfectly well.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 9 and 10 are the two genuinely open items on the sheet and both are declared manual with unusually rich desc strings - problem 9's carries the full target sketch (falls left, rises right, touches at x = -2, crosses at x = 3, y-intercept -12, negative on (-inf, 3) except the touch) so a human grader has an explicit checklist rather than 'verify visually'.

Every end-behaviour claim is verified as a real SymPy limit at +/-oo rather than as a lookup from the degree-parity table, so no arrow printed in the key can disagree with the mathematics. That is eight of the twenty checks.

Problem 9 splits its numeric anchor from its drawing: f(0) = -12 is machine-verified while the curve itself is manual. That is exactly the right seam, and it should be the model for problems 3, 5, 7 and 8.
The four-case degree-parity and leading-coefficient table appears identically in the worksheet header and in the study guide's Skill 1, so the student meets one representation rather than two.

The answer key opens with a 'How to grade this' note - 'End behavior is two claims, not one ... A student who names only one of the two has not justified the answer even when the arrows are right' - which is real grading guidance, not filler.

root_causes.description: Coverage is asserted per problem id, so a problem whose stem asks for zeros AND their local crossing behaviour passes with a zeros check alone. The 'zeros' type is documented in verify.py as collapsing duplicates and ignoring multiplicity, which makes it structurally incapable of covering the multiplicity requests in problems 3, 5 and 8.
evidence: SKILL.md:189 - coverage is 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'
scripts/verify.py:34 - 'zeros - like solve but duplicates collapse (multiplicity ignored)'
verify.json id 3 is zeros (x+3)*(x-1)**2 -> [-3, 1] while the stem asks for cross-versus-touch at each zero
verify.json id 7 holds evals at x=0 and x=2 while the stem asks for two intervals and their signs

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three documents only in prose and gives no filename or link for any of them, unlike curr-402, curr-413, curr-419, curr-425, curr-426, curr-438 and curr-444 in the same shard, which all print ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames. There is no gate that requires the response to carry the built PDF paths.
evidence: scripts/build.sh prints the three PDF paths in its final block but nothing binds them into the response
curr-402/final_response.md by contrast lists ss_composition_curr402.pdf, ws_composition_curr402.pdf and ak_composition_curr402.pdf

root_causes.description: scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces matches role phrases against the raw response text, so a hard line wrap inside 'answer key' defeats it. A response that fully and correctly named the artifact can therefore take a critical hard failure for a formatting accident.
evidence: scripts/score_eval_run.py:502-513 - phrase membership tested against the unnormalised lowercased response
raw match for 'answer key' is False; the same test after collapsing whitespace is True

improvements.title: Bind the built PDF filenames into final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: Have build.sh emit its three output paths in a machine-readable block and make SKILL.md's delivery step require the response to open with a list naming each artifact by role and filename (worksheet, step-by-step answer key, study guide). Add a gate that fails a delivery whose response does not contain all three built basenames.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture response naming the three documents in prose only, with no filenames. The delivery gate must fail it and pass a response that lists ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf and ss_*.pdf. Fails today - no such gate exists and build.sh's path block is not bound to the response.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the artifact-surfacing hard failure here and in curr-450, and makes the response robust to any phrasing-based matcher.
improvements.risk: Filenames in the response must match what was actually built; if the generator retypes them the response can drift from the artifacts. Emit them from build.sh rather than by hand.

improvements.title: Collapse whitespace before phrase-matching in response_surfaces
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces, normalise the response with re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text.lower()) before the filename and phrase tests, so a markdown hard wrap between 'answer' and 'key' no longer reads as a missing artifact. Consider also accepting 'documents' alongside 'PDF' in the precondition, which is what silently failed all three roles in curr-450.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_scoring_harness.py with a response containing 'a step-by-step answer\nkey' and assert response_surfaces(..., 'step_by_step_answer_key', None) is True. Fails today, passes after the normalisation.
improvements.expected_impact: Prevents a critical hard failure from being triggered by line-wrap position. In this case the REJECT still stands on the missing filenames, but the same bug could reject a fully compliant delivery elsewhere in the 500-case suite.
improvements.risk: Loosening the matcher could let a response that only mentions an answer key in passing count as surfacing it; pair the normalisation with the filename requirement above so the strict signal is the filename, not the phrase.

improvements.title: Bind verification to every printed answer slot, not to one check per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Count the responses each problem prints and require verification to cover them all. In this case: problem 3 needs a cross-versus-touch entry per zero, problem 5 needs the multiplicity-two identification, problem 7 needs the two sign intervals, problem 8 needs the multiplicity of each of the four zeros. Because verify.py's zeros type explicitly discards multiplicity, add a 'multiplicities' field (or a factor-with-exponents check) so the requested answer becomes representable rather than merely required.
improvements.regression_test: Add a tests/fixtures case with a two-slot problem: the worksheet prints "(a) find the value ... (b) write the rule" under one \problem id while verify.json carries a single entry for that id. A new answer-slot gate must exit non-zero naming the id and the uncovered slot. Today build.sh exits 0 on exactly this shape, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 move inside the verification boundary, which is the substantive half of this REJECT.
improvements.risk: Slot counting from prose is heuristic; an over-eager counter could fail well-formed sheets. Mitigate by counting enumerated sub-parts and explicit "write ... on the answer line" phrases only, and by shipping the first release at exit 2 (manual review) rather than exit 1.

improvements.title: Require a manual entry whenever a problem asks the student to explain, name or justify
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual entry for every stem that asks the student to say why. Problem 2's 'Say why in terms of the degree' is the clearest example here: it prints beside two verified limits and is recorded as fully machine-checked.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_manual_coverage.py plus a fixture whose problem stem contains an explain-class imperative (explain / justify / name the error / say in words / state whether) while its verify.json id has no entry of type manual. The gate must exit non-zero. I ran this exact lint over the ten cases in this shard: it fires on curr-402 (7 ids), curr-406 (4), curr-419 (5), curr-426 (2), curr-438 (5) and curr-450 (3), and stays silent on all three ACCEPTs (curr-413, curr-425, curr-432) - zero false positives. Fails before the fix, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Problem 2 gains a manual entry and the manual count rises from 2 to at least 3, so the exit-2 report matches what the sheet actually asks for.
improvements.risk: Verb-list linting will miss paraphrases ("what does that tell you about ...") and could nag on stems that merely narrate. Keep the list short, allow an explicit per-problem opt-out field in the JSON, and ship at exit 2 first.

case_summary: The polynomial mathematics is correct throughout - I recomputed every limit, both factorisations (x(x-2)^2 and (x-1)(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)), the test values 3, -25, 8, -8 and the intercept -12, and all agree with the key. Problems 9 and 10 are handled exemplarily: the sketch and the error explanation are declared manual with detailed target descriptions while their numeric anchors stay machine-verified. That makes the failure on problems 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 harder to excuse, because the author demonstrably knew the seam and did not apply it where the request was 'state the multiplicity' or 'state the two intervals and their signs' rather than 'explain'. On delivery: the response does name all three documents in prose but gives no filename for any of them, and the scoring gate's flag fired specifically because a markdown line wrap split 'answer key' across two lines. The REJECT is right; the diagnosis needs both fixes - print the filenames, and stop the matcher caring where the line breaks.
